narrative.northStar: The Keynote Stage in season liveries, wall to wall (rounds 8 to 10)
narrative.overview:
Each season's robot is launched the way a hardware company launches a product: the machine alone on an almost-black stage, lit from above, standing on a thin floor line. Then the page steps out into calm white and aluminium-grey reading pages that explain the robot, the people, the outreach and the partners.

**Season liveries, wall to wall (round 10; Andy: "i think you can make the entire pages color scene with some respect to the ftc colors").** Every FTC season has a game, and FIRST gives each game a colour palette of three or four colours and black. Every page wears one game's palette from its header to its footer, the way a race car wears a livery that is repainted each year: the site-wide pages wear this season's game (BIOBUZZ: yellow, pale yellow, gold), and each season's page wears its own game (DECODE: mint, vermilion, slate teal; INTO THE DEEP: blue, pale blue, yellow). The two pages that show all three games side by side, home and Seasons, keep the black stage as their head, so the three colours stand on black. A livery fills six jobs: the field (page heads and closing calls: one flat colour with black type, as on the opening's title card), the ground (the alternate bands), the line (box outlines), the mark (the signal: the sponsor action, "next", the controls that move things), the tag (above headings) and the glow (the colour as type on black, in the footer). FIRST Tech Challenge's own orange marks the programme where it is named: "FTC team 26413" on the home stage and the last row of every page. Round 9 (Andy: "reference the mclaren page and build more interactive and somewhat colorful page") had put one colour per season on a few blocks, about 1.5% of the screen as on McLaren's page; round 10 puts the palettes on the page. Beyond the liveries, colour comes from the robots, the photos, the Mercury logo (kept as-is) and, on the partners page, the four sponsorship tiers in the colours of their names (Andy, 2026-11-09: "the sponsorship category should be the color of the tier name"); the budget donut is grey.

Three grounds carry the site. The stage (near-black: the home launch, the partners tier chart and budget donut, the footer, the photo viewer), the field (the page's game colour, flat, with black type: every inner page head, every season head with its robot standing straight on it, the strip that closes the home stage, and the closing "join or partner" bands on the home, team and partners pages) and the reading ground (white, with bands in the livery's pale colour where aluminium grey used to be). Sections run the full width of the page and are separated by a change of ground, never by hairlines. Since round 7 (Andy: "reference the VulcanForms website") the things inside a section are boxes drawn like the cells of an engineering spec sheet: white, a 1px line in the livery's line colour and square corners (Stage Step with a light line on the stage, white with a black line on a field). Nothing floats: the rounded panels on a grey ground from round 6 were removed because Andy said they looked "so AI". Buttons are square, and nothing casts a shadow except a robot on its floor (the only other shadows are the small lift under the chosen outreach year and the halo around the part markers). One family, Archivo, does everything; robot names are set extra wide (125%).

The neutrals are plain: black, white and greys with no colour of their own (until round 10 they leaned violet, from the logo's outline, which fought the yellow). The reference study of Apple, TechCrunch, Vogue, The New York Times Company and Prada specifically warned against reusing Apple's exact greys (#F5F5F7, #A1A1A6) and its 28px cards, which is why the values and radii here differ.
keyCharacteristics: Three grounds: the near-black stage (home launch, partners sheets, footer), the field in the page's game colour with black type (page heads, closing calls), and white with pale livery bands for reading.

Season liveries, wall to wall: every page wears one FTC game's official palette (this season's on the site-wide pages, each season's on its own page), always as flat solid colour; FIRST Tech Challenge's orange marks the programme in two places. Robots, photos and the logo carry the rest; the four sponsorship tiers wear the colour of their names; the budget donut is grey.

Archivo only: page and section headings in capitals at 108% width and 700 (a lighter second line where the heading has a natural one), 125% width at 700 for robot and game names, sentence-case nav and text links, tabular figures for every number.

Full-width sections; every item (a write-up, a member, a program, a season, a post, a table, a tile) is a white box with a 1px line in the livery's line colour and square corners. Square buttons, no section hairlines, no shadows (except the floating header bar once the page scrolls, and the open menu).
Selection shown as light: the chosen bay's field is lit in its season's colour, the others hold a deep shade of theirs; a chosen story row turns white with a signal-colour marker.
One authored opening (the line-up title card, once a visit) and one load moment on the stage; everything else answers a click, tap, drag or key. Nothing moves, fades, pins or changes while scrolling.

rules.name: The Season Livery Rule
rules.body: Every colour on a page comes from FIRST's palettes: the page's own game for its field, ground, line, mark and tag; another season's main colour only where that season is shown; FTC orange only where the programme is named. Colour is always flat and solid: a whole field with black type, a whole band of the pale ground, a block, a bar, a tag or an arrow. Never a gradient between two colours, never a tint behind single cells or columns of a table, never coloured text on white, never a new hue for links or highlights. Violet stays out (Andy found it AI-like).

rules.name: The Keyline Rule
rules.body: Every block of the signal colour carries an ink keyline (a 1.5px ink border or inset line), as the yellow shapes in the BIOBUZZ logo do. It keeps a light colour's edge clear on white and on the pale ground (yellow on white is 1.3:1 without it) and is invisible on the stage. What is white on a field has a black line too: the header bar, the fact tiles, the boxes of a closing band, a photograph. Fields that run the full width (heads, bands) and the bays on the stage have no keyline: they are surfaces, not controls. A field that is a box on white (a row of the Seasons page) keeps the box's line, in black.

rules.name: The Light Still Leads Rule
rules.body: On the stage, emphasis is light: the chosen bay is lit, the others turned down. On light pages it is ink and weight; the signal colour marks actions and the current thing, never ordinary links or text.

rules.name: The Spec Box Rule
rules.body: Sections are full-width bands (white, the livery's pale ground, a field or the stage); every inner page head is a field. Inside a section, each item is a box: paper fill, 1px `--box-line` (the livery's line colour: gold, slate teal or blue), `--r-md` corners (0 since round 8), on white and ground bands alike; on the stage, Stage Step with a 1px light line (`--box-line-stage`); on a field, white with a black line. Inside a box, quotes and chips are filled with the ground colour and photo frames are white, never boxed again (css/style.css "Boxes"). The footer is a stage band that closes every page: the field's 8px stripe on its top edge, its headings in the livery's glow colour, and FTC orange as its last row.

rules.name: The Metals Name The Tiers Rule
rules.body: Each sponsorship tier wears the colour of its name, on its header block (ink text on it), the ticks in its column and its tag on a sponsor card. Nothing else on the site takes a metal: the column washes stay neutral, the budget donut stays grey, and text never wears one.

rules.name: The Width Is The Voice Rule
rules.body: Robot and game names go widest (125%, 700). Page and section headings go uppercase at 108%, in two weights where the heading has a natural first line. Reading text, nav and links stay at normal width in sentence case.

rules.name: The Fixed-Place Figures Rule
rules.body: Every date, amount, spec and result uses tabular lining figures (`<time>` and `.num` get them automatically; spec, facts, figures, budget and season-fact values set them).

rules.name: The Flat Tile Rule
rules.body: Boxes, menus and buttons never cast shadows, and a box never holds another box: inside a box, quotes take a flat fill of the ground colour, chips are white with the box line, and photo frames are white.

dos: Do change colours, sizes, radii and spacing in `:root` in `css/style.css`, never in a component rule.

Do use the stage for the home launch, the partners tier and budget sheets and the footer; a field (the page's game colour, black type) for page heads (the Seasons page keeps the stage: it shows all three games), season heads and the closing call to join or partner; put everything else on white or the livery's pale ground.
Do run sections the full width and put each item (a write-up, a member, a program, a season, a post, a table) in a white box with a 1px `--box-line` border, 6px corners and 16–24px padding.

Do keep every corner square, and end buttons and text links with the drawn arrow (none on mail links and submit buttons, a down arrow on downloads); use `.btn` on light and `.btn--light` / `.btn--outline-light` on the stage.

Do set robot and game names at 125% width and 700, page and section headings uppercase at 108% (split into two weights with `<span class="lite">` only where the heading has a natural first line), and everything else, nav and links included, at normal width in sentence case.
Do give every date, amount, spec and result tabular figures.
Do show a chosen state as light (brighter, full colour, filled dot) and write it to the URL when it is a view someone might share.

Do take every colour from FIRST's palettes (the page's game, another season's colour where that season is shown, FTC orange where the programme is named), and re-point the six `--lv-*` tokens rather than colouring components one by one.
Do set type on a field in black, and give anything white on a field a black line.

Do keep the signal colour to its fixed places, always as a solid block with an ink keyline and black text. The colour is type in two places only, both on black: the header's black button on the yellow pages, and the footer's headings.
Do let the visitor drive anything that moves: buttons, drag, swipe, keys. Give every gesture a button and a key.
Do let new content simply be there: no entrance animation for anything below the first screen.
Do set `--w` to the image's pixel width on every `.photo`.
Do keep the sponsor strip in every footer, built from `SPONSORS` / `SUPPORTERS` in `js/main.js`.
Do add raster images only as the team's own photos or CAD renders, and record how any edited one was made (Assets and Provenance below).
donts: Don't add a hue beyond FIRST's palettes (the three games and FTC orange) and the tier metals; no purple or violet accent, no neon on black. Don't use FTC orange for anything but the programme's two marks.
Don't copy Apple's exact neutrals (#F5F5F7, #A1A1A6) or its 28px cards; use the tokens here.
Don't separate sections with hairlines; change the ground instead. Lines draw boxes and sit inside data, nowhere else.

Don't put shadows on boxes or buttons (the floating header bar's scrolled shadow and the open menu are the exceptions), round a corner, put a box inside a box, or float sections as rounded panels on a grey ground.

Don't colour the budget donut or tint the tier columns, and don't use weak tints, gradients or pill-shaped controls (Andy, 2026-11-09, on colour mockups with one accent on pill buttons and tinted table columns: "just dont do the color it looks terrible"). The tier metals he asked for later the same day; the season colours came with round 9, when he asked for a "somewhat colorful" site after McLaren's; whole fields and bands in the games' palettes came with round 10, when he asked for the colour scheme of the entire page to respect the FTC colours.
Don't add a second font family or system display faces.
Don't put small text labels (eyebrows) above headings or number the seasons 01/02/03; the 28×8px tag is the only mark above a heading, and it never goes on a heading inside a box.
Don't add new load animations outside the stage, counters that tick up, anything that moves by itself (a carousel that advances, a ticker), or motion that ignores reduced motion.
Don't generate or invent images, results, sponsors or numbers; leave "TBD" instead.
Don't show a photo larger than its own pixels.
